NKE.rationale: NKE scores at the extreme negative end of the range because all three pillars align bearish. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Revenue is flat ($11.28B Q3 FY2026, +0.1% YoY) while profitability is in severe decline — operating income collapsed to $650M (5.8% margin vs 7.5% year-ago), net income fell 34.5% to $520M, and operating cash flow cratered 76% YoY to $430M. ROE has halved from 0.322 to 0.16. Gross margin compressed ~120-130 bps to 40.2%, with tariffs alone costing ~3 percentage points. The cash conversion deterioration (OCF yield falling from 8.5% to 3.8%) signals earnings quality erosion beyond what the income statement shows. Pillar 2 (valuation): At 29.8x trailing P/E, the stock yields only 3.4% — below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.46% — meaning the market is paying a premium multiple for a business whose earnings power is actively eroding. P/B compression from 6.4x to 4.75x is mechanically explained by the ROE halving, not a value dislocation. The stock has declined 44% from its 52-week high, but the multiple remains elevated on depressed and deteriorating earnings. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The Q4 FY2026 earnings report on June 30 is a dated catalyst, but it carries downside risk — Greater China revenue guided down ~20%, RBC just downgraded citing 3% growth vs 6% industry average, and the CFO transition adds execution uncertainty. The near-term catalyst tilts negative, reinforcing the bearish score. Structural headwinds (tariffs at $1.5B annualized, agile competitors like On +40% and Hoka +24% taking share, China structural decline) compress margins and slow recovery to 2027+. The franchise is durable enough to survive, but at this valuation with this trajectory, the risk-reward is extremely unfavorable.
